title: Representing algorithms: decision tables, pseudocode, flowcharts and code
goal: Express one decision in words, a table and statements.

prerequisites.text: You know remainders and input/output. This step explains if and comparison.

sections.title: From the task to an operation
paragraphs: 8 is even because division by 2 leaves no remainder. Decision table: remainder 0 → even, remainder 1 → odd. Pseudocode is a human-readable description: “find the remainder; if zero, output even; otherwise output odd”.

In the code, % computes a remainder, == compares values, if selects an action when the condition is true and else when it is false. Parentheses hold the condition; braces hold the branch’s statements. Only one of the two branches executes. We use nonnegative integers here.

sections.title: Express one decision in words, a table and statements.
trace: Set the number from the table.
The first branch prints even; the odd branch is skipped.

sections.title: Change one condition and check the prediction
paragraphs: Replace 8 with 7 and match the new path to the table.

sections.title: When the result differs
paragraphs: Replacing == with != changes the meaning: 8 prints odd. Words, table and code must describe the same rule.

sections.title: Now solve your own task
paragraphs: Classify 14 as even/odd, then check 15. Write the rule in words for both cases before coding.
Practice contains a separate starter. Predict the result before changing your program. Returning to the example does not replace your source.

selfcheck.prompt: What output follows the specified change? Replace 8 with 7 and match the new path to the table.
selfcheck.feedback: 7 has remainder 1 when divided by 2. 1 == 0 is false, so else executes.

selfcheck.prompt: Classify 14 as even/odd, then check 15. Write the rule in words for both cases before coding.
selfcheck.feedback: Compare the output with the readable reference case below. Explain each change using the objects or operations in this topic. 14 must produce even and 15 must produce odd. Replacing == with != in the remainder check incorrectly produces odd for 14.

terms.definition: A readable description of algorithmic steps without a single language's concrete syntax.
A table pairing relevant conditions with their expected actions.
A diagram of actions and branches linked by directed connections.
A record of the evolving program state through execution steps.
